title: Reserve lifecycle credits — smoothing model and enterprise SLA alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: enterprise customers buying reserved GPU capacity report friction when utilization fluctuates across quarters. They want predictable unit economics and contractual SLAs, but also the ability to absorb short-term spikes without overpaying. Current reserved contracts are binary (use vs lose) or rely on inflexible surge credits that are hard to forecast.

Goal: design a reserve lifecycle credit system that (1) smooths value across the commitment period, (2) gives deterministic fallbacks into SLA tiers, and (3) reduces churn by converting partial unused commitment into transferable/buffer credits. We aim to test: conversion rates, moral hazard effects, billing clarity, and legal/compliance acceptance.

Scope: product + pricing experiment to define packaging, a pilot contract addendum for 3 mid-market customers, new billing primitives (credit ledger + API), and console-facing reporting. Engineering will need a low-risk billing integration and quota enforcement. Legal/Finance must approve contract language. Security needs a review for ledger integrity and audit trails.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot contract signed by 3 customers and instrumented in billing
Credit ledger shows correct vesting/decay behavior in sandbox for >= 90 days
No regression to p99 billing latency in integration tests
Legal signoff on sample amendment and SQ responses
success_metrics: Net revenue retention change (delta) after 6 months
Percent of reserved GPU hours converted to credits per quarter
Customer-reported satisfaction (CSAT) for billing clarity >= 4/5 in pilot
Reduction in support escalations about overages by 30% in pilot accounts
proposed_models: Soft-vest: unused reservation vests into transferable credits on a linear schedule (quarterly)
Decay-smoothing: credits decay slowly if not consumed to prevent indefinite liabilities
Brokered-conversion: option to convert unused credits into burst credits at a discounted rate via a marketplace fee
pricing_hypothESIS_and_LEvers: Conversion rate options (50% / 75% / 100% of unused value) — test revenue vs retention tradeoff
Decay windows (6/12/18 months) — test customer behavior & liability exposure
Marketplace fee (5% vs 10%) for transferable conversions — test economics vs churn prevention
SLA tier mapping: credits can be redeemed into higher-latency tiers or burst lanes with different p99 targets
billing_and_instrumentation_requirements: Credit ledger table with immutable events (issue, redeem, decay) and transaction IDs
APIs for issuing and redeeming credits with idempotency keys
Billing reconciliation view per invoice to show credit adjustments
Telemetry for conversion events, redemption latency, and refused redemptions
legal_and_contract_considerations: Amendment template language for reserved capacity credits
Clear definitions for vesting, decay, and transferability
Liability cap on outstanding convertible credits in FY
Tax/accounting treatment guidance from Finance (deferred revenue implications)
security_requirements: Audit trail retention 7 years for convertible credit transactions
KMS signing for ledger events to prevent tampering
RBAC for issuing/redeeming credits in Console and API
ux_and_design_notes: Console: single-pane view for reserve lifecycle with calendar of vesting events
Invoice: human-readable line items showing credit conversions and remaining balance
Popup modal to explain decay schedule at purchase time
pilot_plan: Select 3 customers across sectors (SaaS, fintech, gaming) with differing utilization patterns
30-day pilot onboarding window with contract addendum and sandbox invoicing
Weekly check-ins and biweekly metric reviews with data exports
risks_and_mitigation: Accounting complexity — mitigated by Finance working on a reconciliation helper report
Moral hazard (customers under-provisioning) — mitigated by minimum utilization floors and staged conversion discounts
Legal pushback on transferability — fallback to non-transferable decay model for affected contracts
